title: When Someone Is Missing
description: Twelve minutes to be with missing someone. Grief is love with nowhere to go.

segments.say: Find a place where you can be quiet for a few minutes. Close your eyes, if you like.
There is nothing to fix here. This practice is only for being with what you feel.
Start by feeling the breath. If it is short or caught, that is fine.
Place a hand on your chest, if you like. Feel the warmth of your own hand.
Grief is love with nowhere to go. It hurts this much because the love was this big.
Bring to mind who is missing. A person, an animal, or even a life you used to have.
Let the image come however it comes. The face, the voice, a moment together.
Notice where the missing shows up in the body. The throat, the chest, the belly.
You do not need to change anything. Just let the pain have room.
If tears come, let them come. They belong here.
Notice that grief comes in waves. Sometimes stronger, sometimes lighter.
You do not need to hold back the wave. It rises, and it falls. Breathe with it.
Now, if you can, silently say to the one who is missing whatever you want to say.
It might be thank you. It might be I am sorry. It might be just I miss you.
What you shared is not erased. It goes on in you, in the way you love and see the world.
Now offer a little care to yourself. You are carrying something heavy.
May I be gentle with myself while I miss them.
May I let grief take the time it needs.
May I remember I am not alone in this.
So many people, right now, are missing someone. You are one of them.
Slowly come back to the breath. To the hand on your chest.
When you are ready, open your eyes, without hurry.
